A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the memorization capacity of a neural network is not a function of its size, but a function of its architecture.

we have shown that deep neural networks with Gaussian weights can memorize a dataset with a number of neurons and weights that is only a constant factor larger than what is required by a single-layer neural network.

we prove that deep threshold networks with binary or integer weights can achieve a separation between the memorization capacity and the separation capacity, while Gaussian weights cannot achieve such a separation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
deep neural networks with binary and integer weights can memorize datasets with exponentially smaller capacity compared to networks with Gaussian weights.
, in order to achieve the optimal memorization capacity of deep neural networks, it is not necessary to use Gaussian random weights in all layers.
deep neural networks with binary or integer weights have the capacity to memorize almost as well as networks with Gaussian weights.
